title: Chinese Team Wins 2026 ACM Gordon Bell Prize for Exascale Quantum Chemistry - HPCwire

Off the Wire Press Releases

Chinese Team Wins 2026 ACM Gordon Bell Prize for Exascale Quantum Chemistry

First Exascale Classical Solution Promises New Insights into One of the Most Consequential Chemical Reactions on Earth

CHICAGO, Nov. 19, 2026 – ACM, the Association for Computing Machinery, named a ten-member team drawn from Chinese institutions as the winner of the 2026 ACM Gordon Bell Prize for their project “Closing the FeMo-Cofactor ‘Quantum-Advantage’ Gap with Exascale Supercomputers.” The ACM Gordon Bell Prize tracks the progress of parallel computing and rewards innovation in applying high-performance computing to challenges in science, engineering, and large-scale data analytics.

In biochemistry, FeMo refers to the process by which nitrogen is converted into ammonia, a necessity for the growth of plants and other organisms. The effort to understand the intricate structure and function of this process is often called the FeMo Cofactor (FeMoco) CAS problem.

One way scientists have tried to tackle this challenge is by using high-performance computers to simulate the extremely complex interactions that make FeMo possible, including the interplay of atoms, molecules, and electronic states at the quantum level. It is believed that these simulations will yield insights that will benefit many other disciplines, including agriculture and medicine.

This year’s Gordon Bell Prize-winning team is recognized for developing the first “exascale” classical solution to the FeMoco CAS problem. Exascale computers, the world’s most powerful supercomputers, can perform at least a quintillion (a billion billion) floating-point operations per second.

In the abstract of their paper, the team outlines the technical details of their achievement: “The resulting code has been tuned for two exascale supercomputers, LineShine and China’s New-generation Intelligent Super-computer (CNIS), reaching sustained performance on 20,480 LineShine nodes of 1.456 EFLOP/s in double precision (58.9% of the machine peak) and 5.626 EFLOP/s in mixed precision.”

The members of the ACM Gordon Bell Prize-Winning team are Honghui Shang, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei; Zhiyu Xiao, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing; Zhuozhao Xia, Hao Wu, and Huan Ma (all of University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei); Yongqing Chen and Bin Li (both of the National High Performance Computer Engineering Technology Research Center, Beijing); Zhenyu Li, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei; Yutong Lu, Sun Yat-Sen University, Shenzhen; and Jinlong Yang, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei.

The ACM Gordon Bell Prize was presented today during the International Conference for High-Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis (SC26) in Chicago, Illinois.

About ACM

ACM, the Association for Computing Machinery, is the world’s largest educational and scientific computing society, uniting educators, researchers, and professionals to inspire dialogue, share resources, and address the field’s challenges. ACM strengthens the computing profession’s collective voice through strong leadership, promotion of the highest standards, and recognition of technical excellence. ACM supports the professional growth of its members by providing opportunities for life-long learning, career development, and professional networking.

About the ACM Gordon Bell Prize

The ACM Gordon Bell Prize is awarded each year to recognize outstanding achievement in high performance computing. The purpose of this recognition is to track the progress over time of parallel computing, with particular emphasis on rewarding innovation in applying high performance computing to applications in science. The prize is awarded for peak performance as well as special achievements in scalability and time-to-solution on important science and engineering problems and low price/performance. Financial support for the $10,000 awards is provided by Gordon Bell, a pioneer in high performance and parallel computing.
